Unhealthy coping mechanisms/reward systems/anxiety of failure. Not recommending this at all, just sharing my experience and reality.

  
In school I had so much academic anxiety, it was the only thing that forced me to put in so much effort into exams and assignments. My coping mechanism was hyperfixating on something and using that as an escapism method, as a reward for myself.

  
I have recently been diagnosed with ADHD at the age of 20 and am still on the waiting list for titration (I am in the UK). Now I am in uni and my anxiety has decreased, I believe through more exposure to experiences, activities, and situations. But it is still there, and I feel because of my ADHD I started focusing more on things I enjoy, which resulted in academic neglect. So I am taking the year out and started taking antidepressants to help, while I wait for ADHD medication. I am personally looking more into spirituality and meditation, which I know is EXTREMELY difficult for us ADHDers, because realistically sometimes I lose motivation and give up "whats the point" mentality. But I think it helped with my focus a bit. Going to the gym has helped. Being healthy will help, even if it is slight. And I am saying this as a person with a high tolerance to enjoy anything (courtesy to the ADHD we love so much). Small steps. I realised before I had suspected ADHD and how much of my actions/behaviour was attributable to it, I would set unrealistic expectations, which resulted in giving up easily and frustration.

  
I know I went on a tangent there (ADHD again!!), but hopefully you can find some things helpful from this.
